searchText: Just wondering since I was questioned about this on Discord and we already stumbled upon this opcode a couple of times when doing stuff in a more stateless way: what is the future of the `BLOCKHASH` opcode in a stateless (verkle) world? 🤔 Has this been already discussed or written down somewhere (happy to pointers, no need to rewrite all the stuff here)? So the opocode provides a number -> hash mapping for the last 256 blocks, correct me if I am wrong. Has it been discussed (e.g. in a verkle context, but generally if things go "more stateless") to deprecate this opcode at some point? Or will requested number -> hash block mappings be included in the witness for a block? The two plans I have seen are to include the needed mappings in the witness, or move the mapping into the state trie (so `BLOCKHASH` opcode is basically just an `SLOAD` of sorts). Interesting. Thanks! I highly doubt removing `BLOCKHASH` opcode would be accepted as that would break a number of contracts. <asqyzeron> > <asqyzeron> right, we do not have any support for blockhash in kaustinen. I am adding it as a topic to the next VIC (re @verkle_bot: <holgerd77> Just wondering since I was questioned about this on Discord and we already stumbled upon this opcode a couple of times when doing stuff in a more stateless way: what is the future of the `BLOCKHASH` opcode in a stateless (verkle) world? 🤔 Has this been already discussed or written down somewhere (happy to pointers, no need to rewrite all the stuff here)? So the opocode provides a number -> hash mapping for the last 256 blocks, correct me if I am wrong. Has it been discussed (e.g. in a verkle context, but generally if things go "more stateless") to deprecate this opcode at some point? Or will requested number -> hash block mappings be included in the witness for a block?) <asqyzeron> but for applications that are currently available, as long as you statelessly execute all blocks, you can save the block hash of each block I see. For a stateless execution of blocks that would mean though that a client would always need to wait for 256 blocks to pass until a safe all-contract execution becomes possible. Which is likely not the final state of what we want. Thanks for putting it on the call agenda! Other topic: Was trying to find some basic information about the new verkle testnet https://verkle-gen-devnet-2.ethpandaops.io/ (what has changed? When did it start? Something like that, so: from a only-half-following perspective). The linked "Network Spec" https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/verkle-gen-devnet-2 though returns a 404. Would be good if we can move to add some base testnet info like this (if not already there somewhere) so that it get's a bit easier to follow up. Good place might also be a short README addition here (?) https://github.com/ethpandaops/verkle-devnets/tree/master/network-configs/gen-devnet-2 . //cc <@412614104222531604> we launched it last friday, and didn't have time to catch up on all the different bits and pieces yet. Will be working on a similar spec sheet as what we did for dencun . Thanks a lot, sorry, not meant as an impatient note, great that it will be added! 🙏 🙂 shouldn't return a 404 now, and it should give you a good indication about the spec changes (which was none, compared to the previous testnet.) We decided to do a rename, to be able to keep track of the number of different devnets, and make it easier to follow in case there is a relaunch. Let me know if you got anymore questions. Reminder: Verkle Implementers Call tomorrow (Nov 28th) at 14:00 UTC Add agenda items: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/902 Call link will be shared here in channel

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content:
Just wondering since I was questioned about this on Discord and we already stumbled upon this opcode a couple of times when doing stuff in a more stateless way: what is the future of the `BLOCKHASH` opcode in a stateless (verkle) world? 🤔

Has this been already discussed or written down somewhere (happy to pointers, no need to rewrite all the stuff here)?

So the opocode provides a number -> hash mapping for the last 256 blocks, correct me if I am wrong.

Has it been discussed (e.g. in a verkle context, but generally if things go "more stateless") to deprecate this opcode at some point? Or will requested number -> hash block mappings be included in the witness for a block?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The two plans I have seen are to include the needed mappings in the witness, or move the mapping into the state trie (so `BLOCKHASH` opcode is basically just an `SLOAD` of sorts).

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I highly doubt removing `BLOCKHASH` opcode would be accepted as that would break a number of contracts.

Has this been already discussed or written down somewhere (happy to pointers, no need to rewrite all the stuff here)?

So the opocode provides a number -> hash mapping for the last 256 blocks, correct me if I am wrong.

Has it been discussed (e.g. in a verkle context, but generally if things go "more stateless") to deprecate this opcode at some point? Or will requested number -> hash block mappings be included in the witness for a block?)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <asqyzeron> but for applications that are currently available, as long as you statelessly execute all blocks, you can save the block hash of each block

excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content:
I see. For a stateless execution of blocks that would mean though that a client would always need to wait for 256 blocks to pass until a safe all-contract execution becomes possible. Which is likely not the final state of what we want.

Thanks for putting it on the call agenda!
